steps_h2: How to Make a Staged Product Photo in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Add one product photo, try a few scenes, and download the one you want to post.

steps.d: Add a clear photo of your product. You get a lifelike scene for the store, for social, or for an ad.
Try more than one setting. Keep the scene that shows the item held, worn, or set on a surface.
Pick the scene that fits. Download it for your site, a marketplace, social, or an ad.

faq.a: It places your product in a realistic everyday scene, made from the photo you already have. Shoppers see it held, worn, or set on a table.
You upload a product photo. A scene is built around that item so it looks ready for a store, social, or an ad. You pick the one that fits.

faq.q: Can I use a staged scene on my store?
faq.a: Yes. Download the photo and put it on a product page, a marketplace, social, or an ad.

faq.q: Can I choose the setting for my product?
faq.a: Yes. Name the kind of place you want. If the first scene is not the one, ask for another.

faq.q: Can I change the scene after it is made?
faq.a: Yes. Adjust the background, or make a second scene from the same photo. Add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: What should the source photo show?
faq.a: The whole product, easy to see, with nothing important cut off at the edge of the frame.

faq.q: What does one staged scene cost?
faq.a: One photo is 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Does the scene replace my plain catalog photo?
faq.a: No. Keep the original for small details. Use the scene when you want shoppers to picture the product in use. If the source photo is hard to read, start with [how to take product photos for AI](page:guide-product-photo-tips).

faq.q: Can I post the scene on Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. Use it as the product photo in the feed. Write the caption in Instagram, and add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: Can I use the scene in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Finish the headline and the offer in your ad editor. The photo does not include your price.

faq.q: Can I make another scene of the same product?
faq.a: Yes. Start again with a different place. Each photo is 24 credits, and you see that cost before you start.

platforms.h2: Every Step of a Product Photo
platforms.lead: Make, clean, and resize the photos you sell with, on every channel, from one file to a full catalog.

items.t: Remove the Photo Background
items.d: Lift the product off its old backdrop and drop in a clean studio setting that shows it clearly.

items.t: Generate a New Background
items.d: Make a custom backdrop, or change the color, and keep the look of your brand.

items.t: Create a Lifestyle Scene
items.d: Help shoppers picture the product in use by setting it in an everyday scene.

items.t: Fix Light, Clutter, and Size
items.d: Adjust the brightness, clear a stray object, and resize the file for the channel that needs it.

items.t: Show the Product on an AI Actor
items.d: Show how it looks worn or held by an AI actor, so shoppers can judge the scale.

items.t: Download a File You Can Post
items.d: Export a photo that is ready for your site, a marketplace listing, or an ad.

items.t: Improve Lighting and Color
items.d: Even out the light, the detail, and the color before you build a scene on top.

items.t: Resize for a New Shape
items.d: Go from a tall frame to a wide one, or the other way, and keep the product intact.

items.t: Send Scenes From Your Catalog
items.d: Connect the catalog and request a scene for each product, without opening every file by hand.

items.t: Add a Short Line on the Photo
items.d: Place a short message on the photo, in a style that fits the shop. The price still goes in your ad editor.

items.t: Apply One Look to Many Photos
items.d: Give a stack of photos the same backdrop or the same size in a few clicks.

items.t: Share Scenes With Your Team
items.d: Pass a scene and a note to the person who owns the product page, before it goes live.

items.t: Save Logos, Fonts, and Colors
items.d: Keep your mark, your type, and your colors together so the next scene matches.

items.t: Make a Simple Brand Mark
items.d: A new shop can make a simple mark here, then place that mark on the next scene.

items.t: Edit on a Computer or a Phone
items.d: Start the scene on a laptop and finish the crop on a phone.
